newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank says inflation in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank says inflation in line with expectations.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Thursday said inflation was in line with forecasts made in June for an annual rate of inflation of about one percent in 1997 and two percent in 1998.
"Developments do seem to be broadly in line with the assessment in the latest inflation report," the Riksbank said in a statement.
The June quarterly inflation report said the underlying rate of inflation in 1997 and 1998 was estimated to be between 1.5-2.0 percent.
Riksbank deputy governor Lars Heikensten said the situation appeared to be in line with this report.
"It's still too early for a detailed evalutions of all the information of importance for inflation in Sweden that has flowed in during the summer," Heikensten said.
He said a positive feature was the stable situation in international demand. Activity in Europe was turning upwards and the U.S. economy remained strong.
"There is also the prospect of persistently subdued inflation in the world around us," he said.
Heikensten said activity in the Swedish economy picked up in the second quarter after a weak start to 1997.

Domestic demand appeared to be recovering. Households had increased their purchases of durable goods, consumers were becoming more optimistic, and investment was turning upwards. Both export and imports were rising strongly.
"The Swedish economy still has unutilised resources. This is an important reason why we can have relatively good growth that is compatible with low inflation," Heikensten said.

He said business sector productivity was rising in a way that was favourable to inflation. Since June. the crown's exchange rate in terms of the Trade Currency Weighted index has appreciared a couple of percent.
Preliminary figures show the rate of wage increases has slowed since the summer of 1996.
The bank's next inflation report will be published on September 23.
